input.quote: 14.2 Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
input.rationale: Section 14.2 vests exclusive ownership of every Deliverable created specifically for Customer (defined in 1.4 to include work product) in Vendor, and gives Customer only a revocable, non-transferable licence limited to the Order Form term. That fails the fallback on every material term — the licence is revocable, not perpetual, not worldwide, not royalty-free, and carries no modification or sublicensing right — so it is a material deviation rather than a minor shortfall. The rest of the IP architecture is already acceptable: 14.1 confirms Customer owns Customer Data and other Customer material, 14.3 leaves Vendor its pre-existing Vendor Technology, 13.2 grants a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to Vendor Technology embedded in a Deliverable, and 14.4 disclaims joint ownership. The shortest cure is therefore to reverse the direction of ownership in 14.2 only, which reaches the preferred position without collateral rewrites; the deleted licence sentence is not cross-referenced elsewhere (10.1 preserves rights in accepted Deliverables "according to their terms").

proposal.summary: Reverse Deliverable ownership in 14.2 so Customer owns and Vendor assigns each Deliverable.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We own what we pay for, so we have reversed Section 14.2: Customer owns each Deliverable created for it and Vendor assigns its rights, replacing the revocable, term-limited licence. Vendor keeps its pre-existing Vendor Technology under Section 14.3 and the Section 13.2 perpetual licence still covers anything embedded; if outright ownership is not possible, our fallback is a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense Deliverables.

ops.newText: Customer exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer, and Vendor assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest in each Deliverable.
